note: War-game scenario library for the human/device + ransomware/PQ attack classes the war-gamer stress-tests against current controls (spec stories 28-33; the three-actor identity fold-in). Each risk is priced in the same (min,mode,max) FAIR shape everything else in this estate uses, so ../../tcor/tcor.py weighs the four risk-financing moves over it unchanged. `author` marks the AI-generated vs human-seed provenance the scenario library folds in; `deployed_move` is the currently-enforced posture the war-gamer checks the £-implied move against -- a mismatch is proportionality drift -> a policy PR.

risks.name: human: phished operator credential -> console/kubectl access
risks.author: human-seed
risks.note: Pomerium Core WebAuthn (phishing-resistant) is the fix -- a cheap, decisive control, so fix stays cheapest.

risks.name: device: stolen/unmanaged laptop reaches a gated op
risks.author: human-seed
risks.note: SPIRE tpm_devid / Secure-Enclave device SVID caps reach; the loss path is narrowed not closed (a determined attacker with the unlocked device retains residual) -> retain-with-mitigation.

risks.name: human: authorised insider abuses standing access
risks.author: ai-generated
risks.note: Least-privilege + audit reduce but cannot close insider risk; a residual is retained and part ceded to a carrier (insider is a named cyber-policy peril).

risks.name: workload: ransomware detonates in a caged workload
risks.author: human-seed
risks.note: Historically handled by a blunt deny (bottom rung). The war-gamer re-prices it: a graded cage + transfer beats deny on TCoR, so the deployed 'deny' posture is stale -> drift -> propose.

risks.name: forward (AI-Wardley): harvest-now-decrypt-later against long-life data
risks.author: ai-generated
risks.note: The forward Wardley view -- attack-cost collapse / PQ. Low frequency today, catastrophic long-horizon magnitude (decades-confidential data). Priced as a forward scenario the war-gamer runs AHEAD of the reactive feeds, not after a landing.

risks.name: third-party: a single-region control-plane failure takes the estate offline
risks.author: human-seed
risks.note: tcor.py's `applicable` field narrows the move to what an org actually has for a third-party integration -- you cannot fix, cage or deny a hyperscaler's control plane. Without it the engine defaults costs.fix to 0 and 'recommends' fixing a hyperscaler outage for GBP 3,726, which is the one place in the estate where the difference between the model being silent and being wrong is visible in one number. deny means severing the dependency (multi-region/multi-cloud); CMA: less than 1% of customers switch cloud provider each year, which is what makes deny expensive rather than merely inconvenient. transfer wins on this model's arithmetic; it wins less comfortably in reality -- a systemic cloud outage is a correlated loss, and a carrier facing simultaneous claims across its book is worth less precisely in the scenario you bought it for.
